newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Albright in Slovenia to smooth ground on NATO.
newsitem.headline: Albright in Slovenia to smooth ground on NATO.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright arrived in Slovenia late on Friday for a one-day visit to smooth ruffled feathers after the country was left out of the first wave of NATO expansion this week.
Albright was met at Ljubljana airport by Slovenian Prime Minister Zoran Thaler and was due to meet Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek and President Milan Kucan on Saturday.

She is expected to encourage the former Yugoslav republic to continue to pursue its democratic reforms and its bid for NATO membership despite U.S. insistence Slovenia and Romania should not be included in the alliance's first expansion round.
Only the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland were invited to join the 16-nation military alliance.
"I expect Mrs. Albright to explain the U.S. standpoint towards NATO enlargement," Drnovsek told a news conference on Friday.
He said the visit was expected to deal also with bilateral relations.
"The U.S. obviously wants to deepen its relations with Slovenia. They do not want relations to worsen (over the NATO decision)," Drnovsek said.
Slovenia expected to be invited to join NATO in the second round of its expansion which was likely to be determined in 1999, he said.
Albright is scheduled to leave Slovenia at 1130 GMT on Saturday.
